text:
Maria G: Pushed a quick eval pack for Lyambda's customer LoRA merge. Seeing weird token-boundary artifacts after int4 quant. Sample below.

Sam K: can you paste the sample outputs?

Maria G: Input: "Invoice total: $1,234.56"\nBaseline (float16): "Invoice total: $1,234.56"\nMerged LORA + int4: "Invoice total: $1234 .56"  <-- token split inserted space after comma

Cheng L: hmm looks like tokenizer mismatch / merge alignment. Did the adapter change tokenizer config?

Maria G: Adapter shouldn't touch tokenizer. It's a classic token-boundary split when we pack KV cache across quantized weights. Repro steps:
```bash
# repro script (shortened)
python eval_pack.py --model lyambda-base:2026-02-17 --adapter lyambda-cust-lora-v2 --quant int4 --prompt-file samples.csv
```

Olivia R: Any diffs in vocab or added tokens? Could be special tokens appended during fine-tune.

Maria G: No new tokens. I ran tokenizer.debug() — alignment maps are identical pre/post. But logits at boundary show strange spike around comma.

eval-bot: Regression scan (quick-eval) — precision metrics: token-split rate +6.8% vs baseline, BLEU -0.4, exact-match -2.1%

Sam K: +6.8% split rate is non-trivial for invoices. Could be quant kernel rounding + LoRA interplay.

Cheng L: Try running with per-channel scaling disabled / try s8 quant profile to see if it persists. Also test with KV cache disabled (warming off) to rule out caching quantization bug.

Maria G: Good plan. Quick results: disabling KV cache (cache=False) -> split rate drops to +1.2% (almost baseline). So cache + int4 + adapter seems to trigger it.

Olivia R: If cache is the culprit, fallback policy for customer could be set to use float16 cache or force cache off for invoice route until we patch.

support-bot: Noted. Created ticket INF-1293 and assigned to eng-runtime. Customer PM notified.

Sam K: For patch path: 1) reproduce unit test for token-boundary in quantized cache; 2) test alternative reorder of KV dtype conversion; 3) run longer eval with invoices.

Maria G: I'll open a small repo with repro and add failing test. Tagging @Cheng L for kernel review.

Cheng L: I'll look into kernel quant->dequant sequence. Might be small off-by-one when merging LoRA deltas into packed weights during compile.

Maria G: Thanks. If anyone grabs hotfix, add a canary rollout to cust Lyambda with cache=off until we verify.

Olivia R: I'll prepare canary policy in Console: route=lyambda-invoice -> model-variant fallback to float16-cache if split-rate >3%.

Sam K: Great. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
